entries.footer/tagline: The AI-native CMS layer for Next.js.
entries.home/cta/subtitle: Self-host it, or try the free preview.
entries.home/features/body: The schema is defined in code and generated back as types, so a wrong content key is a compile error rather than a blank section.

home/features/items.body: Paste one prompt. Your coding agent installs the packages, creates the account and keys, and uploads the schema.
home/features/items.title: Set up by your agent

home/features/items.body: Define content next to the components that render it. Run ainam pull and the types come back down.
home/features/items.title: Code-first schema

home/features/items.body: Upload once. Format is read from the file header, never the filename, and the URL is resolved per request.
home/features/items.title: Images and assets

home/features/items.body: Every publish is a version. Roll back a single key or a whole publish.
home/features/items.title: Version history

home/features/items.body: Drafts are readable through their own credential and their own path, never the site key.
home/features/items.title: Preview before publish

home/features/items.body: A boolean field switches a whole section off. No deploy, no feature flag service.
home/features/items.title: Section toggles

home/features/items.body: Every entry carries a language and falls back to the default. The dashboard edits the default language today; translations go in through the API.
home/features/items.title: Locales as data

entries.home/features/title: Content that lives beside your components
entries.home/hero/announcement/text: Roll back a publish from the dashboard
entries.home/hero/body: Tell your coding agent to add AINAM, or install three small packages yourself. Text, images and whole sections of your Next.js site become editable in a dashboard, with no redeploy.
entries.home/how/body: AINAM ships as three small npm packages. The key in your environment points the site at a project, and the project holds all of its content.

home/how/steps.body: The client has no dependencies of its own, and the Next.js adapter adds only that.
home/how/steps.title: Install the packages

home/how/steps.body: The content schema lives in your codebase. Push it, and pull the types back down.
home/how/steps.code:
$ npx ainam push
$ npx ainam pull
home/how/steps.title: Push your schema

home/how/steps.body: Text, images, rich text and whole sections — changed, previewed, published.
home/how/steps.title: Edit from the dashboard

entries.home/publish/body: Every change is a draft. Preview it on the real site, publish when it reads right, and roll the whole set back if it does not.
entries.home/publish/title: Nothing reaches the site until you say so
entries.meta/description: Tell your coding agent to add AINAM. The text, images and sections of your Next.js site become editable in a dashboard, without a redeploy.
entries.meta/title: AINAM — the AI-native CMS layer for Next.js
